newsitem.title: UK: Army, police probe suspect object in N. Ireland.
newsitem.headline: Army, police probe suspect object in N. Ireland.

text.p: Troops and police, on heightened alert against a new wave of IRA guerrilla attacks, were sent to Northern Ireland's south Armagh border country on Friday to examine a suspicious object.

Security sources said what appeared to be oil containers with wires leading from them were sighted near derelict buildings outside the village of Cullyhanna. The area was sealed off by police and troops.

The alert was called 24 hours after security forces disarmed what they said was a 1,000-lb (500-kg) bomb abandoned by the Irish Republican Army in the grounds of Belfast Castle because of a tight security cordon in the provincial capital.
Police said the device was intended to be used for "mass murder" of security forces by the IRA, which is fighting to end British rule of Northern Ireland to reunite it with Ireland.
They said it appeared to herald a New Year's offensive by the IRA which is demanding the inclusion of its political wing, Sinn Fein, in Northern Ireland peace talks.
Earlier in the day controlled explosions were carried out on a vehicle abandoned in the car park of a Belfast pub. It was thought to have been used in a robbery and deemed suspicious, police said.
Britain and Ireland, co-sponsors of the peace negotiations, say the IRA must call a halt to violence and pledge a commitment to peaceful means to take part in the talks.
The IRA's foes, so-called Loyalists who want the province to say British, are taking part in the talks by virtue of having stuck by a ceasefire since October 1994.
